subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: picks up the brain's tiny voltages — millionths of a volt — from the scalp or ear canal.

subsystems.name: Analog front end
subsystems.role: turns microvolt signals into clean digital data without drowning in noise.

subsystems.name: Stimulus and task protocol
subsystems.role: gives every session the same conditions so recordings can be compared.

subsystems.name: Feature extraction
subsystems.role: reduces a noisy waveform to a compact signature.
parts: artifact rejection for blinks and muscle activity

subsystems.name: Matcher
subsystems.role: compares a live recording with the enrolled template and accepts or rejects.

subsystems.name: Liveness and anti-spoofing
subsystems.role: checks that the signal comes from a living person present at the sensor.

subsystems.name: Template store
subsystems.role: holds the biometric reference securely and allows it to be revoked.

buildSteps.title: Choose the neural response
buildSteps.detail: Decide whether to read spontaneous rhythms at rest or a response evoked by a stimulus. A useful signature must be repeatable across days, not just within one sitting.

buildSteps.title: Build the headset
buildSteps.detail: Place electrodes at fixed, documented positions on a comfortable headset or earpiece, with stable skin contact and low contact impedance.

buildSteps.title: Record enrolment sessions
buildSteps.detail: Capture several sessions from each volunteer on different days and at different times, so the template includes natural variation rather than one lucky recording.

buildSteps.title: Clean and featurise
buildSteps.detail: Remove eye-blink and muscle artifacts, filter the signal, and extract the features that will represent a person.

buildSteps.title: Train and validate the matcher
buildSteps.detail: The test must be cross-session: enrol on one day, verify on another. Within-session accuracy flatters brain biometrics and is not the number that matters.

buildSteps.title: Add liveness checks
buildSteps.detail: Show that a recorded or synthesised signal is rejected, and that the enrolled person must actually perform the task.

buildSteps.title: Protect the template
buildSteps.detail: Store a transformed version of the signature so that a leaked database cannot be replayed, and the template can be cancelled and reissued.

buildSteps.title: Trial in a controlled setting
buildSteps.detail: Deploy on a small, consenting group and track accuracy over months, since the signature can drift with fatigue, caffeine, medication or illness.

prerequisites.tech: Wearable EEG sensors with stable contact
prerequisites.why: dry and in-ear electrodes exist, but good contact without gel still degrades over a session.
brain signals are tiny, so amplifier noise and mains interference set the ceiling on accuracy.
most published work uses small groups recorded once, so long-term stability is not measured.
brain signals cannot be changed like a password, so a secure revocable template is essential.
without reliable liveness detection a recording can be replayed to the sensor.

pathway.milestone: laboratory studies identify individuals from resting or evoked brain activity with high within-session accuracy
pathway.unlocks: proof that a neural signature carries identity information at all.

pathway.milestone: shared multi-session datasets and standard protocols
pathway.unlocks: honest measurement of how much accuracy survives weeks and months.

pathway.milestone: ear-EEG and fusion with liveness or a second factor
pathway.unlocks: unobtrusive, continuous authentication from a wearable rather than a lab headset.
a practical high-security access method — or the field stays a research niche used only where nothing cheaper will do.
